description: Patients qualify if they have a record with a urine protein result of '-' and a record with a rheumatoid factor result of '-'. These can be different records.

a.request: Consider patients who have at least one laboratory record with a urine protein (`U-PRO`) result of exactly '-' and at least one laboratory record, not necessarily the same one, with a rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result of exactly '-'. For each such patient, use all of their laboratory records to compute the average prothrombin time (`PT`) and the average of `TAT` minus `TAT2`. Across these patients, what are the average of the per-patient PT averages and the average of the per-patient TAT − TAT2 averages? Give them as a single row with these two values, unrounded, and ignore missing values at every step.
a.sql: WITH qualifying AS (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN `U-PRO` = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN RA = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0), per_patient AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.TAT - l.TAT2) AS avg_tat_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN qualifying q ON l.ID = q.ID GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_of_avg_pt, AVG(avg_tat_diff) AS avg_of_avg_tat_diff FROM per_patient;

b.request: Across patients who have at least one Laboratory record with `U-PRO` = '-' and at least one Laboratory record with `RA` = '-' (possibly different records), compute each patient's average `PT` and average `TAT - TAT2` over all their Laboratory rows (ignoring NULLs), then return the unrounded average of those per-patient PT averages and the unrounded average of those per-patient TAT − TAT2 averages as one row.
b.sql: WITH eligible AS (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN `U-PRO` = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN RA = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0), per_patient AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.TAT - l.TAT2) AS avg_tat_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN eligible e ON l.ID = e.ID GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_tat_diff) AS avg_tat_diff FROM per_patient;
b.raw: Across patients who have at least one Laboratory record with `U-PRO` = '-' and at least one Laboratory record with `RA` = '-' (possibly different records), compute each patient's average `PT` and average `TAT - TAT2` over all their Laboratory rows (ignoring NULLs), then return the unrounded average of those per-patient PT averages and the unrounded average of those per-patient TAT − TAT2 averages as one row.

c.request: Consider patients whose laboratory results include a urine protein (`U-PRO`) result of exactly '-' and a rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result of exactly '-'. For each such patient, use all of their laboratory records to compute the average prothrombin time (`PT`) and the average of `TAT` minus `TAT2`. Across these patients, what are the average of the per-patient PT averages and the average of the per-patient TAT − TAT2 averages? Give them as a single row with these two values, unrounded, and ignore missing values at every step. Patients qualify if they have a record with a urine protein result of '-' and a record with a rheumatoid factor result of '-'. These can be different records.
c.sql: WITH qualified AS (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN `U-PRO` = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN RA = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0), per_patient AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.TAT - l.TAT2) AS avg_tat_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN qualified q ON l.ID = q.ID GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_of_pt_averages, AVG(avg_tat_diff) AS avg_of_tat_diff_averages FROM per_patient;

d.request: Patients with at least one lab record where U-PRO = '-' and at least one (possibly different) record where RA = '-' qualify; for each, average PT and TAT−TAT2 over all their lab records, skipping nulls, then average those per-patient values across patients and return both unrounded in one row.
d.sql: WITH qualified AS (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN `U-PRO` = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN RA = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0), per_patient AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.TAT - l.TAT2) AS avg_tat_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN qualified q ON l.ID = q.ID GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_tat_diff) AS avg_tat_minus_tat2 FROM per_patient;
